subject: Hybrid endpoint SLA — Time-to-first-token & sustained token-rate proposal
body:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Barnes <elliot@brightpath.ai>, Kate Lin <kate@brightpath.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hybrid endpoint SLA — Time-to-first-token & sustained token-rate proposal

Hi Elliot / Kate —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed, BrightPath's product needs strict first-frame responsiveness for interactive flows while also supporting large, batched generation for nightly jobs. To keep production predictable we sketched an operational SLA addendum for hybrid endpoints (streaming fronted by synchronous fallbacks) that balances TTFT expectations with sustained token/sec guarantees. Draft attached (SLA-draft-ttft-addendum-v1.pdf).

High level proposal (summary):
- Measure TTFT as server-side time from request ingress to first byte emitted to client. Redwood proposes a 95th percentile TTFT target of 250ms for the interactive tier on dedicated capacity.
- Sustained token/sec: guarantee 100 tokens/sec sustained per concurrent request on the dedicated plan, measured as a 1-minute rolling average; bursts up to 600 tokens/sec allowed for short windows (<= 10s) with automatic burst credits.
- Fallback behavior: when capacity constraints occur, requests will degrade to a compatible model variant (smaller topology) with notification headers and a documented latency delta.
- Billing: burst consumption beyond the credit pool billed at an overage rate; pilot customers get initial burst credits.

Asking BrightPath to confirm whether the 95p/250ms and 100 tokens/sec baseline match your expectations, and whether the proposed shorter burst window (10s) is acceptable or if you need a longer smoothing window.

I'll loop in Jonas for the measurement definitions and Marissa for operational runbooks. If this outline looks OK, we can circulate a redline-friendly PDF for procurement.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: SLA-draft-ttft-addendum-v1.pdf

Thanks for the outline and the attachment. Quick questions from the BrightPath side:
1) Can we tighten TTFT for a small subset of critical requests (we have synapse-level calls that gate UI rendering)? For those flows we'd prefer 150ms 95p if possible.
2) For 'sustained token/sec' semantics: what is the enforcement window? Is the 1-minute rolling average per request or per user session?
3) If you fall back to a smaller model variant, will the token accounting change (i.e., will we be billed differently for the same client request)?

Also looped in procurement/legal (Kate + legal@brightpath.ai) — we'll need the exact failure modes and an example runbook to get internal approval. Can PR/ops provide sample telemetry so we can calibrate our client-side retry/backoff?

Subject: Re: Hybrid endpoint SLA — Time-to-first-token & sustained token-rate proposal

Elliot, Ava —

Wanted to add technical definitions so we have the same instrumentation:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): measured server-side from the moment the request headers are accepted by the API gateway to the first 512-byte chunk successfully written to the client socket (includes model kernel scheduling + initial KV fetch). This aligns to how we emit stream frames.
- First-token vs first-chunk: for models that emit many small tokens rapidly we use the first-chunk abstraction (first non-empty write); for metric consistency the SLA references first-chunk 95p.
- Measurement windows: TTFT P95 computed over the request type and route, using a 24-hour rolling window for SLA reporting. Sustained token/sec is calculated per request as a rolling 60s average (tokens emitted / 60s) and we expose 60s and 300s aggregates for diagnostics.
- Throttling: we use gradual shedding at the request granularity — if the endpoint's pool hit sustained utilization > 85% for 60s, new streaming requests will be enqueued briefly then either forwarded to a smaller model variant or served with a reduced token emission cap.

Practical implication: we can hit 150ms P95 for a very small subset if you commit to reserved capacity and pre-warmed containers for that route. Otherwise 250ms P95 is achievable on dedicated pools with warm buckets. I'll attach our internal dashboard link for a recent pilot so you can see actual distributions.

Jonas Weber
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Barnes <elliot@brightpath.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:14:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid endpoint SLA — Time-to-first-token & sustained token-rate proposal

Elliot / Kate —

Operational notes and mitigations we've used successfully for other customers:
- Dedicated 'interactive' slot: carve out a small pool (N GPUs) pinned to your interactive route so the scheduler never mixes heavy batch jobs with low-latency traffic. This is the only reliable way to hit 100–150ms P95 at scale.
- Prewarm + keepalive: maintain a small pool of warmed model instances for the interactive tier; costs are predictable and we can size the pool based on 95p concurrency.
- Burst credits & smoothing: provide an initial burst credit pool for the pilot (we've proposed 10k tokens/day as a pilot credit). Bursts are consumed at emission time; once exhausted, we apply graceful degrade policies (throttle, fallback to smaller model, or queue).
- Telemetry: we'll add a route-specific trace id in the response headers (X-Redwood-Trace) and provide a short sample telemetry export (token-burst-metrics.csv) for you to validate client-side backoff logic.

Attached: SLA-draft-ttft-addendum-v2.pdf (redlines incorporated) and token-burst-metrics.csv sample.

Next steps we propose:
1) BrightPath confirms whether you need 150ms P95 for an explicit set of routes (we'll produce capacity estimates).
2) Confirm billing preference (burst-credit + overage vs flat premium for dedicated interactive pool).
3) 2-week pilot with production telemetry and a post-pilot review to finalize SLA language.

I'm happy to run the pilot onboarding call with our Ops team.

—Marissa
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0223

Attachments: SLA-draft-ttft-addendum-v2.pdf, token-burst-metrics.csv

Hi Marissa / Ava / Jonas —

Appreciate the clarity and the updated draft. Procurement/legal reviewed the v2 PDF and we are comfortable with the approach in principle. A few asks before we sign:
- Please include a concise "failure modes" appendix listing exact behaviors (enqueue, fallback to smaller model, throttling, error response) and associated client-visible headers/status codes.
- We need an example runbook for an incident where the interactive pool degrades (include steps for rollback, traffic-shifting, customer notification).
- Request a controlled 2-week pilot with the burst-credit arrangement. After pilot we'd like a joint review and then a 30-day notice to flip to committed reserved capacity if metrics meet thresholds.

If you can produce the failure modes appendix and runbook snippet by next Wed (2027-07-07), I can get final signoff from legal and operations. Assuming that timeline, procurement can sign the addendum pending no substantive redlines.

Thanks,
Kate Lin
Head of Procurement, BrightPath AI
kate@brightpath.ai
